frontier.hypothesis: A 68-instruction C body exists in which `val`'s live range crosses the loop back edge without a dead preheader store, satisfying livelen(76) >= 68.
frontier.mechanism: Everything else in the residual is already bought: s19's probe H buys livelen(75) >= 20 for +1 instruction and makes allocno 85 vanish entirely. If some shape pays for H's instruction AND puts a real, consumed value in `val` before the loop, the 8/8 disposition closes. Nineteen bodies say the second half has no semantic reading - every arm consumes the operand byte on the next instruction - but that is an argument, not a measurement.
frontier.next_probe: Search for a semantic reading in which the operand byte legitimately persists across an iteration (e.g. a command whose payload is consumed on the FOLLOWING command, or a repeat/run-length command). Test it against the target bytes first: any such reading must still produce exactly the twelve `sb $a1, 0xXX($a0)` arms and the single `lbu $a1, 0x0($v1)` at .L80032544. If no reading survives that check, livelen(76) >= 68 is unreachable in honest C and the RA channel is closed in closed form.
